title: Diabetes mellitus: type, complications and medication status
question: Assign the ICD-10-CM codes for the patient's diabetes, its complications and related long-term drug use.
note:
Chief Complaint
Follow-up for type 2 diabetes and recent hypoglycemia.

HPI
The patient is a 67-year-old male presenting for a follow-up regarding his type 2 diabetes mellitus. He reports that he has been managed on oral hypoglycemic therapy for several years. During this interval, he experienced a hypoglycemic episode while at home. He describes feeling shaky and lightheaded for approximately thirty minutes before consuming a snack. He denies any loss of consciousness or severe symptoms during the event. He continues to adhere to his current medication regimen but seeks guidance on managing these occurrences.

Medication List
Metformin 1000mg twice daily.

Exam
The patient is a well-appearing male in no acute distress. He is alert and oriented. Vital signs are stable. Physical examination reveals no acute abnormalities.

Assessment
1. Type 2 diabetes mellitus.
2. Hypoglycemia.

Plan
We will continue the current dose of metformin. I will instruct the patient on recognizing early symptoms of a hypoglycemic episode and how to respond. We will monitor his blood glucose levels closely over the next month.

Electronically signed, H. Tanaka, MD, 05/14/2026
explanations: Diabetes with hypoglycemia and no coma documented: E11.649.
Long-term oral hypoglycemic use: add Z79.84.

distractors.why: Hypoglycemia is a complication with its own code.
Z79.84 captures long-term oral hypoglycemic use.
